extracted.intended_audience: members of the public, regulated stakeholders, agency staff, and developers who read, draft, search for, or submit comments on Federal Register documents via FederalRegister.gov
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on using FederalRegister.gov to find, read, cite, save, draft, and submit formal comments on Federal Register documents, plus related site features and developer resources. Covers public inspection, search and citation, accessibility, and drafting resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Site Feedback usage limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: Our “Site Feedback” tool and Federal Register email addresses are only intended for users to submit technical questions and comments on the functionality of the FederalRegister.gov website.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These tools cannot be used to submit comments on rulemaking actions or to petition agencies on public policy issues. The Office of the Federal Register/GPO have no authority or ability to process comments on rulemaking via these site feedback channels; use the document's official comment system (e.g., Regulations.gov) or the site's 'Submit a Formal Comment' feature when available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submit a Formal Comment feature
rubrics_metrics.description: FederalRegister.gov now provides a 'Submit a Formal Comment' feature that lets users comment on a document without leaving FederalRegister.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Previously users were redirected to Regulations.gov; the new feature integrates comment submission on-site. Use the formal comment button on a document page to submit comments where offered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Inspection page preview function
rubrics_metrics.description: The Public Inspection web page on FederalRegister.gov offers a preview of documents scheduled to appear in the next day's Federal Register issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Public Inspection page may also include documents scheduled for later issues at the request of the issuing agency. Use the Public Inspection page to access important or complex documents before their official publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document text — active links behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: When an agency has included links as part of the document text, FederalRegister.gov activates those links using the text in the document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A link may not work if the link in the published document contained an error or if the target website is no longer available. Be aware of potential broken links when relying on embedded links in a published document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document sidebar utility bar features
rubrics_metrics.description: The utility bar runs along the left side of the document and scrolls with you down the page, providing quick access to document utilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the utility bar to access the Public Inspection version and the official electronic format of the published document (via the two bottom icons), print using the printer icon, and share (email, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Website organization into topical sections
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal Register documents are organized into six sections (Money, Environment, World, Science & Technology, Business & Industry, and Health & Public Welfare).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These sections group documents by broad themes to help browsing and discovery; use section organization when exploring documents of broad interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document drafting and research resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Links and resources to support drafting and researching Federal Register documents are provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key resources include the Document Drafting Handbook, Incorporation by Reference (IBR) Handbook, Federal Register Bulletins, Final Guidance on Implementing the Plain Writing Act of 2010 (PDF), PlainLanguage.gov, Thesaurus of Indexing Terms, List of Subjects by CFR Title, and GPO page guidance. Consult these when preparing Federal Register submissions or researching drafting conventions and legal requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plain language and plain-writing guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: FederalRegister.gov links to guidance on plain language and implementing the Plain Writing Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Final Guidance on Implementing the Plain Writing Act and PlainLanguage.gov tools to make documents clearer and more accessible to the public when drafting notices, rules, and explanatory materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search tools and citation search
rubrics_metrics.description: The site offers a basic search box in the main navigation and an advanced search with various options.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can search by citation (for example: '75 FR 12345' or '75 Fed. Reg. 12345'). Use basic search for quick lookups and advanced search for complex queries and filtered results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Saving documents for later (MyFR clippings)
rubrics_metrics.description: FederalRegister.gov allows users to save documents for later via a MyFR feature named 'clippings'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documents can be clipped from a document page or search results by clicking the flag icon; users need a MyFR account to use clippings and access saved documents later.

rubrics_metrics.name: Linking and citation practices
rubrics_metrics.description: There are multiple ways to link to FederalRegister.gov documents and several citation patterns for Federal Register documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The site explains linking patterns and gives examples; choose the linking/citation pattern that matches your preferred usage (direct document URL, citation-based link, etc.) and be consistent when referencing documents in external materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility compliance and PDF accessibility
rubrics_metrics.description: FederalRegister.gov is designed following Section 508 and W3C accessibility design guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The site uses text-based files and Adobe PDF files that are text-accessible via Adobe PDF Tools. The Office of the Federal Register and GPO are committed to assisting people with disabilities; consult the Accessibility page for further assistance and tools.

rubrics_metrics.name: Developer resources and APIs
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal Register data is available via a REST API and associated developer resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bulk XML files, MODS metadata, and interactive API documentation are provided. The site maintains API clients (e.g., a Ruby API client) and the project is open source on GitHub (repositories such as federalregister-api-core). Developers should consult the API docs, available clients, and source code when integrating or analyzing Federal Register data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open source availability of site code
rubrics_metrics.description: FederalRegister.gov is a fully open source project and its source code is available on GitHub.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The repositories include federalregister-api-core (which powers import and API responses) and other repos. Review the source to understand data processing, contribute, or adapt clients for custom workflows.
